_about: Plain-English takeaways for key mantras and stories. Editorial, labelled as such on screen, and never presented as translation.

verses.IU_0: Whole comes from whole, and the whole remains: taking away from the infinite does not make it less. A way to begin from abundance rather than lack.
verses.IU_1: Everything is already held by something greater than you. Enjoy what you have by not grasping, and do not covet what is someone else's.
verses.IU_6: When you see yourself in others and others in yourself, contempt has nowhere to stand.
verses.IU_7: Grief and confusion come from feeling separate; seeing the one in all ends both.
verses.IU_9: Practice without understanding blinds, but cleverness without practice blinds even more.
verses.IU_15: The truth is often hidden behind something golden and attractive. Ask for the cover to be removed.
verses.KeU_1.1: Your mind, breath, speech and eyes all work, but who sets them working? Start by asking the question.
verses.KeU_1.4: What you are looking for is not what words describe, but what makes words possible.
verses.KeU_2.3: Those who are sure they have understood it have not; those who know they have not understood are closer.
verses.KaU_1.1.20: Naciketas refuses to be distracted from the one question that matters: what happens to us at death?
verses.KaU_1.1.27: Money cannot satisfy a person. You can have it and still not have what you came for.
verses.KaU_1.2.2: Every choice offers the pleasant and the good. The wise look at both and choose the good; the careless take whatever feels good now.
verses.KaU_1.2.18: What you truly are was never born and cannot die. The body ends; the knower does not.
verses.KaU_1.2.23: Cleverness and learning are not enough. The Self is revealed to the one who truly seeks it.
verses.KaU_1.3.3: You are the rider; your body is the chariot; your intellect holds the reins of your mind. Do not hand the reins to the horses.
verses.KaU_1.3.4: The senses are horses running toward what they see. Without a driver they choose the road.
verses.KaU_1.3.14: Wake up, and learn from those who have walked the path. It is sharp as a razor's edge: go carefully, but go.
verses.KaU_2.1.1: The senses face outward, so we look outward. A rare person turns around to look within, longing for what does not die.
verses.KaU_2.3.14: When the desires lodged in the heart let go, a mortal becomes free while still alive.
verses.MuU_1.1.4: There are two kinds of knowing: knowing about things, and knowing what makes knowing possible. Both matter; only one frees.
verses.MuU_2.2.4: OM is the bow, your self is the arrow, the Real is the target. Aim without distraction and become one with it.
verses.MuU_3.1.1: Two birds sit on one tree. One tastes every fruit, sweet and bitter; the other only watches. Both are you.
verses.MuU_3.1.6: Truth alone wins in the end, not falsehood. (India's national motto comes from this line.)
verses.MuU_3.2.8: Rivers keep their names until they reach the sea. Freedom is losing a smaller identity into a greater one.
verses.MaU_2: All this is Brahman, and this Self is Brahman: what you are and what everything is are not two.
verses.MaU_7: Beyond waking, dreaming and deep sleep is the awareness that witnesses all three. That is the Self.
verses.TU_1.11: Speak the truth, live rightly, never stop learning; honour your mother, father, teacher and guest. Follow what is blameless, not everything you are told.
verses.TU_2.4: Words and thoughts turn back without reaching it; yet one who knows its joy is never afraid again.
verses.TU_3.1: Bhṛgu asks his father what Brahman is and is told: inquire into that from which everything comes. Learning by finding out for yourself.
verses.AiU_3.1.3: Everything you know, see and feel is lit by consciousness. That consciousness is Brahman.
verses.ChU_6.8.7: The subtle essence of everything is the Self. That is the Real, and you are that.
verses.ChU_6.13.2: Like salt dissolved in water, the Real is invisible but present in every drop.
verses.ChU_7.23.1: Real joy is in the boundless, never in the small. Many of our searches fail because we look for the large in the little.
verses.ChU_8.7.1: The Self is free from evil, age, death, grief, hunger and thirst. It is worth seeking and knowing.
verses.ChU_8.8.4: Virocana left satisfied with the first answer and taught it to others. Satisfaction is not the same as understanding.
verses.BU_1.3.28: Lead me from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to immortality: a prayer for clarity.
verses.BU_1.4.10: I am Brahman. Whoever knows this becomes the whole, and even the gods cannot stand in the way.
verses.BU_2.3.6: Not this, not this: whatever you can point to is not the final truth. Keep looking past every 'this'.
verses.BU_2.4.5: We love others not for their sake but for the Self's sake. Know the Self, and everything is known.
verses.BU_4.4.5: You are what your deepest desire is. As your desire, so your will; as your will, so your deeds; as your deeds, so you become.
verses.BU_5.2.3: The thunder says Da Da Da: restrain yourself, give, be compassionate. One syllable, three lessons, each fitted to the listener.
verses.SvU_4.6: Two birds on one tree, the same image as the Muṇḍaka: the one who tastes and the one who sees.
verses.SvU_6.11: One God is hidden in every being, the witness of every act, the inner Self of all.
verses.KauU_3.2: Indra tells Pratardana: I am breath, the conscious self. Life and awareness are not two different things.
verses.PU_1.2: Before answering, the teacher asks the students to live a year with discipline and trust. Readiness is part of the answer.
